Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] in the
**simple-label case**: $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in
\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ with $v=\|V\|\ge0$, $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on
$D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and $E$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ of
**multiplicity one** with gap at least $g>0$,
$\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let $\psi_{0}$ be a
normalized eigenvector, $P_{0}\psi_{0}=\psi_{0}$, let
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}, \qquad Q_{0}=I-P_{0},$$
be the reduced inverse of the model clause (c)(iii). In the branch $v>0$ put
$$R:=\frac{g}{8v}.$$
Then clauses (a)-(e) hold for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<R$
in this positive-norm branch; clause (f) covers $v=0$ independently of $R$:

(a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; the model's followed label
$E_{\lambda}$ of the contour $|z-E|=g/2$ exists, is the unique spectral value
of $H(\lambda)$ inside that contour, is real, and its spectral projection is
the orthogonal rank-one projection
$P_{\lambda}=E_{H(\lambda)}(\{E_{\lambda}\})$;

(b) the gauge-fixed eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_{\lambda}\psi_{0}}{\langle P_{\lambda}\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle}$$
is analytic in $\lambda$, satisfies $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle=1$
and $(H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)$, and
$$q:=2|\lambda|v/g\le\tfrac14,\qquad \|P_{\lambda}-P_{0}\|\le\tfrac13,\qquad \|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2 ;$$

(c) the model's label identity
$$E_{\lambda}=\bigl\langle (H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\bigr\rangle =E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle$$
holds, so the deviation $\lambda\mapsto E_{\lambda}-E$ of the model's energy
label is controlled by the perturbation alone;

(d) the exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0},\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,$$
with $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^{2}/g$; the
second-order coefficient involves the whole complementary spectral subspace of
$H_{0}$ through $S$, continuum included;

(e) the cubic remainder obeys
$$\left|E_{\lambda}-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^{2}}{2}E''(0)\right| \le \frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^{3}}{1-|\lambda|/R},$$
so at $|\lambda|=R/2$ the bound is $g/32$ and for $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at
most $128v^{3}|\lambda|^{3}/g^{2}$;

(f) if $v=0$, that is $V=0$, then $P_{\lambda}=P_{0}$, $E_{\lambda}=E$ and
$\psi(\lambda)=\psi_{0}$ for every real $\lambda$, and no radius involving
division by $v$ is used in this branch;

(g) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the multiplicity
one of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts no unbounded or
degenerate perturbation theorem, no time-dependent perturbation, and no
statement about which branch of the family a preparation occupies.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the
state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical
suppliers.

**(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair,
fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$
on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the
unperturbed sharp energy observable,
fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with
$$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless:
$\lambda V$ is read in joules). Declare the **perturbed family**
$$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$
to be the model's sharp energy observable at coupling $\lambda$. Since $V$ is
$H_{0}$-bounded with $H_{0}$-bound $0\le a<1$ (the bound inequality holds with
$a=0$ and $b=v$), the Kato-Rellich theorem applies and $H(\lambda)$ is
self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ for every real $\lambda$
([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
This self-adjointness is a supplied theorem about the declared operators; the
reading of the family as the system's energy is the model assumption.

**(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$
of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$
and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The
definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers:

(i) for real $\lambda$ with $2|\lambda|v/g<1$, the **followed spectral cluster** is the spectrum of $H(\lambda)$ inside $|z-E|<g/2$, and
$$P_\lambda:=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z-E|=g/2}(z-H(\lambda))^{-1}\,dz$$
(counterclockwise) is its rank-$r$ orthogonal spectral projection, by [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]]. The cluster is a nonempty finite set and is exactly the spectrum of the restriction to $P_\lambda\mathfrak H$. In the simple case $r=1$ only, write $E_\lambda$ for its unique spectral value; this scalar is the followed perturbed label of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] and is analytic on the valid coupling disk. For $r>1$ no unique scalar label, branch ordering or individual scalar holomorphy is presumed. At $\lambda=0$ the cluster is $\{E\}$ and its projection is $P_0$. If $v=0$, these data are constant for all real couplings, with no radius involving division by $v$.

(ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift
data (joules per unit coupling);

(iii) the **complementary reduced inverse**
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$
is a bounded operator with the displayed exact complementary-domain inverse. For every finite multiplicity $r\ge1$, including $v=0$, its existence follows by applying part (c) of [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]] at coupling $\lambda=0$ and $w=E$: since the cluster projection is then $P_0$, the restriction of $E-H_0$ to $D(H_0)\cap Q_0\mathfrak H$ has a bounded two-sided inverse $R_Q(E):Q_0\mathfrak H\to D(H_0)\cap Q_0\mathfrak H$, and $S=-\iota_{Q_0}R_Q(E)Q_0$. For $r=1$ the same operator is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]. Its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint
operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition
asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no
statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any
eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no
measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the
labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are simple tensors and are the special case in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation. Their finite linear span is dense in $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ by the construction; a pure composite preparation may be any unit ray in this completion, including a norm limit of finite linear combinations of product vectors, and need not factor. General composite preparations are density operators on this space and include the statistical mixtures of clause (iii). A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ with length scale $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, and
the energy-observable content of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le m\le l$ let
$\psi_{nlm}$ be the regular bound solutions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] and put
$\Psi_{nlm}:=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$, and put
$$E_{n}:=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}\qquad(n\ge1).$$
Then:

(a) for every label, $\Psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$, $\|\Psi_{nlm}\|=1$,
$H_{\kappa}\Psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\Psi_{nlm}$, and vectors with distinct labels are
orthogonal; the vectors $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span a subspace of dimension
$\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$;

(b) the eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $E_{n}$, $n\ge1$;
the eigenspace of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ is exactly
$\operatorname{span}\{\Psi_{nlm}:0\le l\le n-1,\ -l\le m\le l\}$, so the model
assigns to the level $n$ the **model degeneracy** $n^{2}$; in particular
$H_{\kappa}$ has no eigenvalues in $[0,+\infty)$, whose spectral content is
entirely essential spectrum $[0,+\infty)$ in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] (a);

(c) the family
$(\Psi_{nlm})_{n\ge1,\,0\le l\le n-1,\,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal
family of the negative spectral subspace
$E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the bound states
span exactly the preparations whose energy outcomes are negative almost surely;

(d) the family is not complete in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the
nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, and every unit vector $\psi$ in it has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$, i.e.
strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero in such a preparation;
consequently the bound states of the model do not exhaust its state space and
the model possesses continuum states which are not bound states;

(e) *Energy-law reading.* For every unit vector $\psi$ the restriction of the
energy outcome law to the negative half-line is the discrete law
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}\delta_{E_{n}}$ with weights
$w_{n}:=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$; for
$\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ the whole law is the point mass $\delta_{E_{n}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The values $E_{n}$ are model
parameters determined by $\hbar,m,\kappa$; no numerical value, no measured
line, no transition rate, no photon or light-matter coupling and no empirical
result is asserted. The absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace
is recorded by the cited mathematics for the unscaled operator and is not
restated for the scaled model here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be as above, let
$(\psi_{nlm})$ be the bound eigenfunctions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]], and for
$i=1,2,3$ define the coordinate multiplication operator
$$Q_i\psi:=(\xi\mapsto\xi_i\,\psi(\xi)),\qquad D(Q_i):=\{\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C):\xi_i\psi\in L^2\}.$$
Write also $Q_0:=x_3$ and $Q_\pm:=(x_1\pm ix_2)/\sqrt2$. Then:

(a) each $Q_i$ is self-adjoint on $D(Q_i)$, the domain is a proper dense subspace of $L^2$, and every bound state satisfies $\psi_{nlm}\in D(Q_i)$, with $\|Q_i\psi_{nlm}\|_2^2=\int_0^\infty r^2|u_{nl}(r)|^2dr\cdot\int_{S^2}|\Omega_iY_{lm}(\Omega)|^2d\sigma(\Omega)<\infty$;

(b) for all labels and each $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ the matrix element $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ is absolutely convergent and factors as
$$\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle=\Bigl(\int_0^\infty r\,u_{n'l'}(r)\overline{u_{nl}(r)}\,dr\Bigr)\Bigl(\int_{S^2}Y_{l'm'}(\Omega)\overline{Q_q(\Omega)\,Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr),$$
where $Q_q(\Omega)$ denotes the restriction of the polynomial $Q_q$ to $S^2$;

(c) the angular factor vanishes unless $l'=l+1,\ m'=m+q$ or $l\ge1,\ l'=l-1,\ m'=m+q$; these are necessary conditions only: no assertion is made that an allowed pair has nonzero radial integral, and no transition probability is asserted or computed;

(d) for the oscillator: with $\omega>0$, $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, the complete orthonormal family $(\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}})$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] and the position operator $X$ (multiplication by $\ell y$ in the scaled variable) one has
$$X\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}^{\mathrm{osc}}+\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}^{\mathrm{osc}}\bigr),$$
so $\langle\psi_{n'}^{\mathrm{osc}},X\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}}\rangle$ vanishes unless $n'=n\pm1$, with the displayed coefficients; in particular the oscillator position matrix elements are supported on a single step $|\Delta n|=1$, while the Coulomb selection rules constrain only $\Delta l$ and $\Delta m$ and leave the radial integral free.

This item concerns matrix elements of multiplication operators on $L^2$ and
their finiteness and selection rules; it asserts no absorption, emission or
transition rate and no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Use the notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]]: $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ with polar measure
$\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), the Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument, the complete orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]],
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks $V_l=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$ and
the finite span $H$, the spaces $H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of complex harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$,
and the polynomial representatives $h_{lm}\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of the $Y_{lm}$, characterized by
$\mathrm{res}_l(h_{lm})=Y_{lm}$ where $\mathrm{res}_l(p)$ is the class of $p|_{S^2}$
([[def-homogeneous-polynomial-and-homogeneous-ideal]], [[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]],
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Put $H_{-1}^{\mathrm{pol}}:=\{0\}$, fix $l\ge0$ and $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$,
write $\mathcal H:=h_{lm}$, and define the three polynomial multipliers
$$Q_0:=x_3,\qquad Q_\pm:=\frac{x_1\pm ix_2}{\sqrt2},$$
so that $Q_q=\sum_{i=1}^3c_{q,i}x_i$ with $c_{0,i}=\delta_{i3}$ and $c_{\pm,i}=(\delta_{i1}\pm
i\,\delta_{i2})/\sqrt2$. Let $D_i$ and $L_z,L_3$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]], where $L_3=L_z$ and $L_zY_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]). Then, for each $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$:

(a) (harmonic decomposition) the polynomial $G_q:=\dfrac{\sum_ic_{q,i}\,\partial_i\mathcal H}{2l+1}$ lies in
$H_{l-1}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ and
$$Q_q\,\mathcal H=R_q+r^2G_q,\qquad R_q:=Q_q\mathcal H-r^2G_q\in H_{l+1}^{\mathrm{pol}},$$
where $r^2(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2$; for $l=0$ one has $G_q=0$ and $R_q=Q_q\mathcal H$;

(b) (degree selection) the function $Q_q|_{S^2}\cdot Y_{lm}$ lies in $V_{l+1}\oplus V_{l-1}$ (with
$V_{-1}:=\{0\}$); consequently, for all $l'\ge0$ and $m'\in\{-l',\dots,l'\}$,
$$\langle Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm},\ Y_{l'm'}\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever } l'\notin\{l-1,\,l+1\};$$

(c) (weight selection) as elements of $H\subset L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ one has
$$L_z\bigl(Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\bigr)=\hbar(m+q)\,\bigl(Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\bigr),$$
because $\partial_\varphi Q_q=iq\,Q_q$ on $S^2$ ([[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]],
[[def-complex-exponential]]); hence in addition
$$\langle Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm},\ Y_{l'm'}\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever } m'\ne m+q;$$

(d) (selection rules) combining (b) and (c): the angular matrix element
$\langle Y_{l'm'},\,Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\rangle$ can be nonzero only if
$$l'=l+1\ \text{and } m'=m+q,\qquad\text{or}\qquad l\ge1,\ l'=l-1\ \text{and } m'=m+q;$$
in particular only $\Delta l=\pm1$ and $\Delta m\in\{0,\pm1\}$ occur with the component-dependent shift
$\Delta m=q$ for the multiplier $Q_q$. These are necessary conditions on the angular integrals only: no
assertion is made that an allowed pair has a nonzero integral, and no absorption, emission or transition
probability is asserted or computed.

Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] in the
**simple-label case**: $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in
\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ with $v=\|V\|\ge0$, $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on
$D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and $E$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ of
**multiplicity one** with gap at least $g>0$,
$\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let $\psi_{0}$ be a
normalized eigenvector, $P_{0}\psi_{0}=\psi_{0}$, let
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}, \qquad Q_{0}=I-P_{0},$$
be the reduced inverse of the model clause (c)(iii). In the branch $v>0$ put
$$R:=\frac{g}{8v}.$$
Then clauses (a)-(e) hold for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<R$
in this positive-norm branch; clause (f) covers $v=0$ independently of $R$:

(a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; the model's followed label
$E_{\lambda}$ of the contour $|z-E|=g/2$ exists, is the unique spectral value
of $H(\lambda)$ inside that contour, is real, and its spectral projection is
the orthogonal rank-one projection
$P_{\lambda}=E_{H(\lambda)}(\{E_{\lambda}\})$;

(b) the gauge-fixed eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_{\lambda}\psi_{0}}{\langle P_{\lambda}\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle}$$
is analytic in $\lambda$, satisfies $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle=1$
and $(H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)$, and
$$q:=2|\lambda|v/g\le\tfrac14,\qquad \|P_{\lambda}-P_{0}\|\le\tfrac13,\qquad \|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2 ;$$

(c) the model's label identity
$$E_{\lambda}=\bigl\langle (H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\bigr\rangle =E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle$$
holds, so the deviation $\lambda\mapsto E_{\lambda}-E$ of the model's energy
label is controlled by the perturbation alone;

(d) the exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0},\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,$$
with $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^{2}/g$; the
second-order coefficient involves the whole complementary spectral subspace of
$H_{0}$ through $S$, continuum included;

(e) the cubic remainder obeys
$$\left|E_{\lambda}-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^{2}}{2}E''(0)\right| \le \frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^{3}}{1-|\lambda|/R},$$
so at $|\lambda|=R/2$ the bound is $g/32$ and for $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at
most $128v^{3}|\lambda|^{3}/g^{2}$;

(f) if $v=0$, that is $V=0$, then $P_{\lambda}=P_{0}$, $E_{\lambda}=E$ and
$\psi(\lambda)=\psi_{0}$ for every real $\lambda$, and no radius involving
division by $v$ is used in this branch;

(g) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the multiplicity
one of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts no unbounded or
degenerate perturbation theorem, no time-dependent perturbation, and no
statement about which branch of the family a preparation occupies.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the
state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical
suppliers.

**(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair,
fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$
on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the
unperturbed sharp energy observable,
fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with
$$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless:
$\lambda V$ is read in joules). Declare the **perturbed family**
$$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$
to be the model's sharp energy observable at coupling $\lambda$. Since $V$ is
$H_{0}$-bounded with $H_{0}$-bound $0\le a<1$ (the bound inequality holds with
$a=0$ and $b=v$), the Kato-Rellich theorem applies and $H(\lambda)$ is
self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ for every real $\lambda$
([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
This self-adjointness is a supplied theorem about the declared operators; the
reading of the family as the system's energy is the model assumption.

**(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$
of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$
and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The
definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers:

(i) for real $\lambda$ with $2|\lambda|v/g<1$, the **followed spectral cluster** is the spectrum of $H(\lambda)$ inside $|z-E|<g/2$, and
$$P_\lambda:=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z-E|=g/2}(z-H(\lambda))^{-1}\,dz$$
(counterclockwise) is its rank-$r$ orthogonal spectral projection, by [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]]. The cluster is a nonempty finite set and is exactly the spectrum of the restriction to $P_\lambda\mathfrak H$. In the simple case $r=1$ only, write $E_\lambda$ for its unique spectral value; this scalar is the followed perturbed label of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] and is analytic on the valid coupling disk. For $r>1$ no unique scalar label, branch ordering or individual scalar holomorphy is presumed. At $\lambda=0$ the cluster is $\{E\}$ and its projection is $P_0$. If $v=0$, these data are constant for all real couplings, with no radius involving division by $v$.

(ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift
data (joules per unit coupling);

(iii) the **complementary reduced inverse**
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$
is a bounded operator with the displayed exact complementary-domain inverse. For every finite multiplicity $r\ge1$, including $v=0$, its existence follows by applying part (c) of [[lem-nrqm-approximations-finite-rank-gapped-cluster-projection]] at coupling $\lambda=0$ and $w=E$: since the cluster projection is then $P_0$, the restriction of $E-H_0$ to $D(H_0)\cap Q_0\mathfrak H$ has a bounded two-sided inverse $R_Q(E):Q_0\mathfrak H\to D(H_0)\cap Q_0\mathfrak H$, and $S=-\iota_{Q_0}R_Q(E)Q_0$. For $r=1$ the same operator is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]. Its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint
operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition
asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no
statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any
eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no
measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the
labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, $l\ge0$,
$k>0$, let $A_l$ be the radial operator of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]], write
$$j:=\frac{\gamma}{2k}-l-1,$$
and for $a=2l+1$ and $n\in\mathbb N_0$ let
$$L_n^{(a)}(x):=\sum_{i=0}^{n}(-1)^i\binom{n+a}{n-i}\frac{x^i}{i!}$$
be the $n$-th Laguerre polynomial of order $a$. Then:

(a) *substitution.* A $C^2$ function $u$ on $(0,\infty)$ satisfies $-u''+(l(l+1)/r^2-\gamma/r)u=-k^2u$ if and only if $v(x):=e^{x/2}x^{-(l+1)}u(x/2k)$ is $C^2$ and satisfies $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $(0,\infty)$;

(b) *regular series.* With $v_0:=1$ and
$$v_{i+1}:=\frac{(i-j)v_i}{(i+1)(i+2l+2)}\qquad(i\ge0),$$
the power series $v(x):=\sum_{i\ge0}v_ix^i$ converges for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and defines a solution of $xv''+(2l+2-x)v'+jv=0$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) *regular solution and general solution.* The function
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r):=r^{l+1}e^{-kr}v(2kr)$$
is a $C^\infty$ solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ with $u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ as $r\downarrow0$; it is, up to a nonzero scalar multiple, the only solution with $u(r)/r^{l+1}$ bounded as $r\downarrow0$; every solution of the radial equation on $(0,\infty)$ is $c_1u_{\mathrm{reg}}+c_2u_2$ with $u_2$ defined near zero by $u_2(r):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)\int_{r_*}^r u_{\mathrm{reg}}(s)^{-2}ds$, where $0<r_*<\delta$ and $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has no zero in $(0,\delta)$, and extended uniquely to $(0,\infty)$ by the regular initial-value equation, and every solution that is not a multiple of $u_{\mathrm{reg}}$ has $|u(r)|/r$ unbounded as $r\downarrow0$;

(d) *termination.* $v$ is a polynomial if and only if $j\in\mathbb N_0$; in that case $v$ is a nonzero constant multiple of $L_j^{(2l+1)}$, and
$$u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)=c\,r^{l+1}e^{-kr}L_j^{(2l+1)}(2kr)\quad(c\ne0)$$
lies in $L^2(0,\infty;dr)$;

(e) *eigenfunction.* If $j\in\mathbb N_0$ then $u_{\mathrm{reg}}\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu_{\mathrm{reg}}=-k^2u_{\mathrm{reg}}$; equivalently, for every $m$ the transported function $\psi(r\Omega):=u_{\mathrm{reg}}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ lies in $H^2(\mathbb R^3)\cap D(C)$ and satisfies $C\psi=-k^2\psi$.

The assertions are statements about the ordinary differential equation and
the operators $A_l,C$; no physical interpretation of $\gamma,k$ or of any
spectral level is made.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis used by the change-of-variables lemma cited below. For every real
$\lambda>0$ and every integer $k\ge0$ the function $r\mapsto r^{k}e^{-\lambda
r}$ is Lebesgue integrable on $(0,\infty)$ and

$$\int_0^\infty r^{k}e^{-\lambda r}\,dr=\frac{k!}{\lambda^{k+1}}.$$

The assertion is an identity for the Lebesgue integral of a nonnegative Borel
function; no probabilistic interpretation and no normalised density are
asserted. In particular no statement is made about any other exponent, about
complex $\lambda$, or about negative powers.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $P_l$ be the Legendre polynomials of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]], and for $l\in\mathbb N$ and $0\le m\le l$ define the
function $w_{lm}:(-1,1)\to\mathbb R$ by

$$w_{lm}(t):=(-1)^m(1-t^2)^{m/2}\,\frac{d^m}{dt^m}P_l(t),$$

where $(1-t^2)^{1/2}>0$ denotes the nonnegative square root. Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ and let the angle coordinates be $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$
([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]). The image of $\Phi$ is
$S^2\setminus C$, where $C:=\{(x,0,z)\in S^2:x\ge0\}$; $C$ is closed and $\sigma(C)=0$ by applying the integral identity of
[[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]] to its indicator. For $l\ge m\ge0$, define the representative
$\widetilde Y_{lm}:S^2\to\mathbb C$ on $S^2\setminus C$ by
$$\widetilde Y_{lm}(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)):=b_{lm}w_{lm}(\cos\theta)\frac{e^{im\varphi}}{\sqrt{2\pi}},$$
and on the cut $C$ by
$$\widetilde Y_{lm}(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta):=b_{lm}w_{lm}(\cos\theta)/\sqrt{2\pi}\qquad(0\le\theta\le\pi).$$
The limits at $\varphi=0$ and $2\pi$ agree because $m$ is an integer, and the endpoint values of $w_{lm}$ from (a) give the limits at the poles; hence $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ is continuous. For $1\le m\le l$ set
$\widetilde Y_{l,-m}:=(-1)^m\overline{\widetilde Y_{lm}}$, and write $Y_{lm}$ for the class of $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) each $w_{lm}$ extends continuously to $[-1,1]$, with $w_{lm}(\pm1)=0$ when $m\ge1$, and on $(-1,1)$
it satisfies the associated Legendre equation
$$-\bigl((1-t^2)w_{lm}'\bigr)'+\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}w_{lm}=l(l+1)w_{lm}\qquad(-1<t<1),$$
equivalently $(1-t^2)w_{lm}''-2tw_{lm}'+\Bigl[l(l+1)-\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}\Bigr]w_{lm}=0$;

(b) for fixed $m\ge0$ the functions $w_{lm}$, $l\ge m$, are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2((-1,1),dt)$:
$\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}w_{km}\,dt=0$ for $k\ne l$; moreover $0<\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt<+\infty$;

(c) with $b_{lm}:=\bigl(\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt\bigr)^{-1/2}>0$ and the representatives just defined, one has
$|Y_{l,-m}|=|Y_{lm}|$ and
$\overline{Y_{lm}}=(-1)^mY_{l,-m}$ for all $l$ and all $m$ with $|m|\le l$;

(d) the family $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l\}$ is orthonormal in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]): for all $(l,m)\ne(l',m')$
with $|m|\le l$, $|m'|\le l'$, the integral $\int_{S^2}Y_{lm}\overline{Y_{l'm'}}\,d\sigma$ equals $0$, and it
equals $1$ when $(l,m)=(l',m')$;

(e) $w_{l0}=P_l$, and $w_{ll}(t)=(-1)^l\frac{(2l)!}{2^l l!}(1-t^2)^{l/2}$.

The functions $Y_{lm}$ are complex-valued $L^2$-functions on the sphere; no physical interpretation as angular
momentum eigenfunctions or spherical harmonics of an atom is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]) and let $(Y_{lm})_{l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l}$ be the
functions of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]] ([[def-complex-exponential]]).
Then $(Y_{lm})$ is a complete orthonormal family of the complex Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]):
the family is orthonormal, and if $F\in L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ satisfies
$\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma=0$ for all $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, then $F=0$ almost everywhere.
Consequently every $F$ has the expansion
$$F=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=-l}^{l}\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle Y_{lm},\qquad \|F\|^2=\sum_{l,m}|\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle|^2,$$
with $\langle F,Y_{lm}\rangle=\int_{S^2}F\overline{Y_{lm}}\,d\sigma$ and finite-subset-net convergence
([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let

$$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$

and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set
([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then:

(a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$
the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle;

(b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$;

(c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue
integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and
imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

derivations.claim: [The compressed matrices and their nonzero entry] Write $a=a_{\mu}$. From [L5], $\|u_{10}\|_{2}^{2}=4a^{-3}2!/(2/a)^{3}=1$ and $\|u_{21}\|_{2}^{2}=(24a^{5})^{-1}4!/(1/a)^{5}=1$; the explicit Kummer solutions therefore give the normalized bound states with the stated labels. For their positive real representatives, $\int_{S^{2}}Y_{10}\Omega_{3}Y_{00}\,d\sigma=(\sqrt3/(4\pi))2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}t^{2}dt=1/\sqrt3$. Their radial dipole integral is $\int_{0}^{\infty}r u_{21}u_{10}\,dr=(1/\sqrt6)a^{-4}4!/(3/(2a))^{5}=256a/(81\sqrt6)>0$. The absolutely convergent factorization [L2] yields $\langle\psi_{210},Q_{3}\psi_{100}\rangle=128\sqrt2 a/243>0$. Since $D_{3}=-qQ_{3}$, its matrix element is $-128\sqrt2 q a/243$ before rephasing. Set $\psi_{1}=\psi_{100}$ and $\psi_{2}=-\psi_{210}$ to obtain the positive off-diagonal value $D_{\rm rel}=128\sqrt2 q a/243$ without changing energies, labels or normalization. By [L2], bound states lie in all coordinate domains; all diagonal entries vanish by degree selection, and the off-diagonal $Q_{\pm}$ entries vanish by weight selection. Thus $D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0$ and $D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\sigma_{1}$ with $D_{\rm rel}>0$, proving (a).

[The two-state family] In the orthonormal basis $(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})$ one has $\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}|_{W}=\operatorname{diag}(E_{1},E_{2})$ by [L1] and orthogonality of distinct eigenstates; with $v:=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\, m^{-1}})$ in joules one has $V=-v\sigma_{1}$ and $$H_{S}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&-v\lambda\\-v\lambda&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}.$$ Since $\sigma_{1}$ is Hermitian with $\|\sigma_{1}\|=1$, $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; the exact eigenvalues of a matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&w\\w&b\end{pmatrix}$ with real $w$ are $\frac{a+b}{2}\pm\sqrt{(\frac{a-b}{2})^{2}+w^{2}}$, verified by the same direct eigenvector computation as in the two-level example of this page with $g:=\Delta$, $w:=-v\lambda$; substituting $a=E_{1},b=E_{2}$ gives clause (b).

[Coefficients] The label $E=E_{1}$ is simple with gap $\Delta$ (the second level is $E_{2}=E_{1}+\Delta$ and there are no further levels in the two-dimensional model); the perturbation $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; hence [L3] applies for $|\lambda|v<\Delta/8$. Since $V$ has vanishing diagonal, $E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle=0$. The reduced inverse on $Q_{0}W=\mathbb C\psi_{2}$ is $S=\Delta^{-1}|\psi_{2}\rangle\langle\psi_{2}|$, so $SV\psi_{1}=-(v/\Delta)\psi_{2}$ and $VSV\psi_{1}=(v^{2}/\Delta)\psi_{1}$, giving $E''(0)=-2v^{2}/\Delta$; substituting $v=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})$ and expanding the closed form of clause (b) by [L4] gives the displayed quadratic Stark shift. This is clause (c).

[The finite remainder check at the true half radius] At $\mathcal E=\Delta/(16D_{\rm rel})$, $\lambda v=D_{\rm rel}\mathcal E=\Delta/16$ and hence $\lambda=R/2$ for $R=\Delta/(8v)$. The page's bound is $Rv(1/2)^{3}/(1-1/2)=Rv/4=\Delta/32$. The exact lower branch satisfies $F_{-}=E_{1}+\Delta/2-\sqrt{\Delta^{2}/4+\Delta^{2}/256}=E_{1}+\Delta(8-\sqrt{65})/16$, whereas its quadratic truncation is $E_{1}-(\lambda v)^{2}/\Delta=E_{1}-\Delta/256$. Therefore $|F_{-}-E_{1}+\Delta/256|=\Delta(129-16\sqrt{65})/256=\Delta/[256(129+16\sqrt{65})]$ by [L4]. Since $129+16\sqrt{65}>128$, this remainder is strictly less than $\Delta/32768$, and consequently less than $\Delta/32$. This proves (d) without a decimal approximation.

[Scope] The argument used the declared two-state truncation, the adopted coupling, the model's exact spectrum and the page's theorem; no laboratory atom, measured shift, polarizability, transition rate or uncompressed linear potential entered. Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary
complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in the first variable,
and let $A=A^*$ be a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$.
There is no separability or supplied-basis hypothesis on $H$.

There is a unique regular projection-valued Borel measure $E_A$ on
$\mathbb R$ representing $A$, with $E_A(\mathbb R)=I$, strong countable
additivity and

$$D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^2d\mu_x(\lambda)<\infty\},\qquad \|Ax\|^2=\int\lambda^2d\mu_x,\qquad \mu_x(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle.$$

Regularity means compact inner and open outer approximation of each finite
scalar measure $\mu_x$. For bounded Borel $b$, its calculus satisfies
$\|b(A)\|\le\sup|b|$, $(bc)(A)=b(A)c(A)$ and
$\overline b(A)=b(A)^*$. For finite-valued, possibly unbounded complex Borel
$b$, there is a closed densely defined operator $b(A)$ on exactly
$\{x:\int|b|^2d\mu_x<\infty\}$, with norm given by that integral and
convergence of the bounded cutoffs on its domain.

The PVM is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$, and a real $\lambda$ belongs to $\sigma(A)$ exactly when every neighborhood of $\lambda$ has nonzero spectral projection. For $z\notin\sigma(A)$, the bounded resolvent is the multiplier $(\lambda-z)^{-1}$, maps into exactly $D(A)$, and has norm at most $\operatorname{dist}(z,\sigma(A))^{-1}$ (with the zero-space convention $1/\infty=0$).

The operators $U_A(t)=e^{itA}$ form a strongly continuous unitary group on
all of $H$, with the exact derivative criterion

$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac{U_A(t)x-x}{t}\text{ exists in }H\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in D(A),\qquad \left.\frac{d}{dt}U_A(t)x\right|_{t=0}=iAx.$$

They preserve $D(A)$ and its graph norm and commute with $A$ on that domain.
The group with this exact generator is unique. PVMs, Borel calculus and
groups transport under unitary intertwiners, and an isometry intertwining
the groups for all real times has a reducing closed range and intertwines
the PVMs. The construction uses countably generated subspaces attached to
each finite tuple of vectors and their uniquely determined compatible
calculus; it does not choose an arbitrary global cyclic decomposition or
an orthonormal basis of $H$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $T$ be a densely defined linear operator on $H$.

- $T$ is **symmetric** when $T\subseteq T^*$, that is, $D(T)\subseteq D(T^*)$ and
  $Tx=T^*x$ for all $x\in D(T)$; equivalently
  $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ for all $x,y\in D(T)$.
- $T$ is **self-adjoint** when $T=T^*$, that is, the domains and the values
  agree.
- $T$ is **essentially self-adjoint** when its closure $\overline T$ is
  self-adjoint; by [[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]] this presupposes
  that $T$ is closable.

**Consequences, with proofs.** These are part of the content of the definition.

1. *A symmetric $T$ is closable.* $T\subseteq T^*$ and $T^*$ is closed
   ([[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]]), so $T^*$ is a closed
   extension of $T$. In particular the closure $\overline T$ exists and
   $\overline T\subseteq T^*$.
2. *The closure of a symmetric operator is symmetric.* If $T\subseteq T^*$,
   the inclusion reversal of
   [[lem-unbounded-adjoint-is-well-defined-and-closed]] applied to
   $T\subseteq T^*$ gives $(T^*)^*\subseteq T^*$, that is
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^*$. Applying it once more to the inclusion
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^*$ gives $(T^*)^*\subseteq(T^{**})^*$, that is
   $T^{**}\subseteq T^{***}$. Since $\overline T=T^{**}$ and
   $(\overline T)^*=T^{***}$
   ([[thm-closable-iff-adjoint-domain-is-dense]]), this reads
   $\overline T\subseteq(\overline T)^*$: the closure is symmetric. (Each
   application is legitimate because the adjoint is defined once its operator
   is densely defined, and $D(T^{**})$ is dense because
   $T\subseteq T^{**}=\overline T$, so that $D(T^{**})$ contains the dense
   domain $D(T)$.)
3. *A self-adjoint operator has no proper symmetric extension.* If $T=T^*$ and
   $T\subseteq S\subseteq S^*$, then $S^*\subseteq T^*$ by inclusion reversal,
   so $T\subseteq S\subseteq S^*\subseteq T^*=T$ and all inclusions are
   equalities.
4. *A self-adjoint operator is closed*, being equal to the adjoint $T^*$ of the
   densely defined $T$, and *an essentially self-adjoint operator has exactly
   one self-adjoint extension*, namely $\overline T$: a self-adjoint extension
   $S$ of $T$ is closed, hence contains the least closed extension
   $\overline T$, and then $S\subseteq S^*\subseteq(\overline T)^*=\overline T$
   by item 2 and symmetry, so $S=\overline T$.

Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and $T$ a linear operator on $H$ with domain $D(T)$. Write $(z-T)x=zx-Tx$ for $x\in D(T)$. The **resolvent set**
of $T$ is
$$\rho(T):=\{z\in\mathbb C:\ z-T:D(T)\to H\text{ is bijective and }(z-T)^{-1}\in\mathcal B(H)\},$$
where $\mathcal B(H)$ is the space of bounded everywhere defined operators on
$H$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); the **spectrum** is
$\sigma(T):=\mathbb C\setminus\rho(T)$. For $z\in\rho(T)$ the bounded operator
$$R_T(z):=(z-T)^{-1}\in\mathcal B(H)$$
is the **resolvent** of $T$ at $z$. This is the library convention used
throughout the page, matching the bounded resolvent of
[[def-spectrum-and-resolvent-of-a-bounded-operator]]: the shift is $zI-T$, with coefficient $-1$ on $T$.

**The resolvent determines $T$ back.** If $z\in\rho(T)$ and $R:=R_T(z)$, then
$D(T)=\operatorname{ran}R$ and $TRy=zRy-y$ for $y\in H$; equivalently
$T=zI-R^{-1}$ with $D(T)=\operatorname{ran}R$, and $R(z-T)x=x$ for
$x\in D(T)$, $(z-T)Ry=y$ for $y\in H$.

**Nonempty resolvent set forces closedness, without the closed graph
theorem.** Assume $\rho(T)\ne\varnothing$ and fix $z\in\rho(T)$ with
$R:=R_T(z)$. Choose a bound $C\ge0$ such that $\|Rv\|\le C\|v\|$.
The map $F(v,w)=w-Rv$ is continuous, since
$\|F(v,w)-F(v',w')\|\le\|w-w'\|+C\|v-v'\|$.
Its zero set $\Gamma(R)=F^{-1}(\{0\})$ is closed. Because
$D(T)=\operatorname{ran}R$ and $(z-T)Rv=v$ for every $v\in H$, the graph of $T$ is
$$\Gamma(T)=\{(x,Tx):x\in D(T)\}=\{(Rv,zRv-v):v\in H\}=\Phi(\Gamma(R)),$$
where $\Phi(v,w):=(w,zw-v)$ is a continuous linear bijection of $H\oplus H$ with
continuous inverse $\Psi(u,v)=(zu-v,u)$, since $\Phi(\Psi(u,v))=(u,z u-(zu-v))=(u,v)$
and $\Psi(\Phi(v,w))=\Psi(w,zw-v)=(v,w)$. A homeomorphism carries closed sets
to closed sets, so $\Gamma(T)$ is closed and $T$ is closed.
No closed graph theorem and hence no choice principle is used here.

For the zero operator on a nonzero $H$, $\rho(0)=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$: the nonzero shifts have inverse $z^{-1}I$, whereas the zero shift is not bijective. If $H=\{0\}$, every shift is the unique bijection of the zero space, so $\rho(T)=\mathbb C$ and $\sigma(T)=\varnothing$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field $\mathbb K$, read in
the real case from [[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and in the complex case from
[[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]]. A linear map
$T:X\to Y$ ([[def-linear-map]]) is a **bounded linear operator** when there is a
real constant $C \ge 0$ such that

$$\|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \qquad \text{for all } x \in X.$$

Any such $C$ is called a **bound** for $T$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

Let $a\in\mathbb C$, $r>0$, and $\gamma(t)=a+r\exp(it)$ for $0\le t\le2\pi$. For every integer $m$,
$$\int_\gamma(z-a)^m\,dz=\begin{cases}2\pi i,&m=-1,\\0,&m\ne-1.\end{cases}$$

Let $a\in\mathbb C$, let $R>0$, and let $f$ be holomorphic on the disc

$$D(a,R)=\{\zeta\in\mathbb C:|\zeta-a|<R\}.$$

If $0<r<R$, $|z-a|<r$, and $\gamma(t)=a+r\exp(it)$ for $0\le t\le2\pi$, then

$$f(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\gamma\frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta.$$
Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

derivations.claim: [Gap and correctly ordered Neumann inverse] By [F1], the spectral support of $H_0$ is $\sigma(H_0)$. For $z\in\Gamma$, $|z-E|=g/2$ and every other spectral point $t$ has $|z-t|\ge|t-E|-|z-E|\ge g/2$. Thus $\|R_0(z)\|\le2/g$. The operator $H_\lambda$ is closed on $D$: if $x_n\to x$ and $H_\lambda x_n\to y$, then $H_0x_n\to y-\lambda Vx$, so closedness of $H_0$ gives $x\in D$ and $H_\lambda x=y$; the domain remains dense. On $D$, $z-H_\lambda=(I-\lambda VR_0(z))(z-H_0)$. Its first factor has the Neumann inverse [F2], since $\|\lambda VR_0(z)\|\le q_\lambda<1$. Therefore the displayed ordered series gives a two-sided inverse with range exactly $D$, and its geometric estimates give (a). Uniform convergence on the circle and each compact coupling subdisk proves norm holomorphy in $\lambda$; local inverse Neumann series give holomorphy in $z$ on the resolvent set. When $v=0$ this series is constant for all couplings.

[Idempotence from two contours] Fix $\lambda\in\Omega_v$. Step 1.1 bounds the inverse uniformly on $\Gamma$, and another inverse Neumann series gives a resolvent annulus around it. Integrals of a holomorphic operator-valued function over concentric circles in that annulus are independent of radius: differentiating $\int_0^{2\pi}f(E+\rho e^{it})i\rho e^{it}\,dt$ in $\rho$ gives the integral of the periodic $t$ derivative of $f(E+\rho e^{it})e^{it}$, hence zero. Take an outer circle for $z$ and an inner circle for $w$. The inverse equations give $R_\lambda(z)R_\lambda(w)=[R_\lambda(w)-R_\lambda(z)]/(z-w)$, and also commutation of resolvents. In its double integral, the first term integrates in the outer variable to the inner projection integral because $\oint dz/(z-w)=2\pi i$; the second integrates in the inner variable to zero because $\oint dw/(z-w)=0$. Compact continuous integrals can be interchanged by norm Riemann sums. Annular independence identifies both circle integrals with $P_\lambda$, proving $P_\lambda^2=P_\lambda$. Resolvent commutation also gives $P_\lambda R_\lambda(z)=R_\lambda(z)P_\lambda$.

[Graph domains, commutation and holomorphy] The identity $H_\lambda R_\lambda(z)=zR_\lambda(z)-I$ makes the contour integrand continuous into the complete graph space of the closed $H_\lambda$. Integrating there proves $P_\lambda H\subset D$ and $H_\lambda P_\lambda=(2\pi i)^{-1}\oint_\Gamma zR_\lambda(z)\,dz=:C_\lambda\in\mathcal B(H)$. On $D$ the other inverse equation gives $R_\lambda(z)H_\lambda=zR_\lambda(z)-I$, so integration gives $P_\lambda H_\lambda=C_\lambda$ there. Thus the range and kernel reduce the operator with its domain. The uniform coupling series makes both $P_\lambda$ and $C_\lambda$ norm holomorphic. Since $H_0P_\lambda=C_\lambda-\lambda VP_\lambda$, the pair $(P_\lambda,H_0P_\lambda)$ is holomorphic into $\mathcal B(H,H\oplus H)$ and takes values in the closed graph of $H_0$; hence $P_\lambda$ is holomorphic as an operator into that graph space. In particular, the finite restriction $A_\lambda$ is well-defined on all of $M_\lambda$.

[Initial projection and rank throughout the disk] At zero coupling [F1] evaluates the resolvent contour as the PVM projection on the real interior; its only unperturbed spectral point is $E$, so this is $P_0$. This evaluation follows by spectral pairings: scalar circle kernels integrate to one inside and zero outside [F3]; norm Riemann sums converge uniformly in the spectral variable, since the spectrum is at distance at least $g/2$ from the circle, allowing interchange with its finite scalar measures. The circle length $\pi g$ and step 1.1 give $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le q_\lambda/(1-q_\lambda)$. If bounded idempotents $P,Q$ have $\|P-Q\|<1$, then $x\in\operatorname{ran}P$ and $Qx=0$ imply $\|x\|=\|(P-Q)x\|<\|x\|$ unless $x=0$; therefore $Q|_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is injective, and the reverse restriction is also injective. For $s,t\in[0,1]$, the inverse equations give $R_{s\lambda}(z)-R_{t\lambda}(z)=(s-t)\lambda R_{s\lambda}(z)VR_{t\lambda}(z)$, hence $\|P_{s\lambda}-P_{t\lambda}\|\le q_\lambda|s-t|/(1-q_\lambda)^2$. Choose an integer $N>q_\lambda/(1-q_\lambda)^2$ and compare the finite path $P_{j\lambda/N}$, $0\le j\le N$. At each adjacent pair the two injections and finite dimension imply equal rank. Starting with rank $r$ proves rank $r$ at $\lambda$, even when the direct distance estimate is at least one. If $q_\lambda=0$ the path is constant.

[All spectral values of the finite restriction are inside] Put $M=M_\lambda$, $A=A_\lambda$, $P=P_\lambda$ and $Q=I-P$. For $z\in\Gamma$, resolvent commutation and the inverse equations give $R_\lambda(z)|_M=(z-A)^{-1}$ on $M$. If $Au=\alpha u$ with $u\ne0$, then $\alpha\notin\Gamma$ by those equations and $R_\lambda(z)u=(z-\alpha)^{-1}u$. The equation $Pu=u$ and its contour definition give winding number one for $\alpha$, so $\alpha\in\Delta$. In a finite basis of $M$, $w-A$ is invertible exactly when its kernel is zero [F3]; thus every spectral point of $A$ is an eigenvalue and lies in $\Delta$. There are at most $r$ distinct such points, since eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent: in a shortest nontrivial relation among them, applying $A-\alpha I$ for one term removes that term and leaves a shorter nontrivial relation. There is at least one: otherwise $(z-A)^{-1}$ is holomorphic throughout a neighborhood of the closed disk, and the scalar Cauchy formula [F3] makes its contour integral zero entrywise, contradicting its integral $I_M$ and $r\ge1$. Here the zero integral follows by applying the Cauchy formula to $(z-E)(z-A)^{-1}$ at $E$.

[Complementary inverse on its exact domain] For $w\in\Delta$ define $B(w)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\oint_\Gamma R_\lambda(z)/(z-w)\,dz$. As in step 3.1 its range lies in $D$. The identity $(w-H_\lambda)R_\lambda(z)=I-(z-w)R_\lambda(z)$ gives $(w-H_\lambda)B(w)=I-P$ on $H$; its right-hand counterpart gives $B(w)(w-H_\lambda)=I-P$ on $D$. Resolvent commutation shows $B(w)$ commutes with $P,Q$. The bounded map $B_Q(w)=QB(w)Q$ therefore maps $QH$ into $D\cap QH$ and satisfies both inverse equations for $w-H_\lambda$ on that exact complementary domain. No assertion that $B(w)P=0$ is needed. The idempotent splitting is $H=M\oplus QH$ and, since $P H\subset D$ and $P$ preserves $D$, its domain splitting is $D=M\oplus(D\cap QH)$. The complementary domain is dense in $QH$, since applying the bounded $Q$ to approximants from the dense $D$ preserves $D$ and approximates every vector of $QH$.

[Exactly the interior spectrum and generalized eigenspaces] If $w\in\Delta\setminus\sigma(A)$, then the bounded operator $(w-A)^{-1}P+B_Q(w)$ maps $H$ into $D$ and is a two-sided inverse of $w-H_\lambda$ by the domain splitting and step 4.2. If $w\in\sigma(A)$, step 4.1 supplies a nonzero eigenvector in $M$, so $w\in\sigma(H_\lambda)$. This proves $\sigma(H_\lambda)\cap\Delta=\sigma(A)$, with its nonempty finite character from step 4.1. For such an eigenvalue $\alpha$ and an integer $k\ge1$, any generalized eigenvector $x\in D((H_\lambda-\alpha)^k)$ has $Qx$ in the complementary iterated domain, because $P,Q$ preserve $D$ and commute with $H_\lambda$. Step 4.2 makes $H_\lambda-\alpha$ injective on the complement; its powers are then injective on their domains, so $(H_\lambda-\alpha)^kQx=0$ forces $Qx=0$. Conversely $M\subset D$ is invariant, so every generalized eigenvector of $A$ is a generalized eigenvector of the full operator. This proves (c), including the exact complementary inverse.

[Real coupling, zero branch and assembly] The bounded-perturbation adjoint identity is $D(H_\lambda^*)=D(H_0^*)=D$, $H_\lambda^*=H_0+\overline\lambda V$: subtract the everywhere-defined bounded term from the adjoint functional to identify exactly the domain of $H_0^*$. Thus $H_\lambda$ is self-adjoint for every real $\lambda$. For real $\lambda\in\Omega_v$, apply [F1] to this operator. Its spectrum misses the circle by step 1.1, so has positive distance from it by compactness of the circle and openness of the resolvent set. The same uniform scalar-kernel/Riemann-sum evaluation as in step 3.2 identifies $P_\lambda$ with the PVM on the real interior, hence an orthogonal spectral projection on the entire cluster. If $v=0$, the norm definition gives $V=0$, all resolvents and projections are constant for every complex coupling, and the exact PVM domain gives $H_0P_0=EP_0$; therefore the restriction is $E I$ and its spectrum is $\{E\}$. Steps 1.1–5.1 give the other assertions for arbitrary $H$ under CC, using only a finite path and finite bases; no individually ordered or holomorphic scalar branches have been introduced.
